text:
sara: Heads-up — we're seeing p95 east-west latency jump to ~120ms between gpu-node-22 and gpu-node-23 during the 09:00-09:30 UTC batching window. Affects a handful of customer queues. Anyone else? :thinking:
amir: Yep, I saw the alert. Noted TCP retransms + a spike in softirq on those hosts. Throwing links to the metric dash: https://grafana.internal/r/dash/ew-latency?panel=22
kevin: Can you paste the `dmesg` / `kernel` logs for those nodes? Suspect NIC driver flapping or RX drop.
sara: Pasting a trimmed log snippet from gpu-node-23: ```kernel: mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: CQ error event: type 17 sc 0 vendor 131 uptime 55234ms
kernel: mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: SRQ error: qp 0x3d4 state 0x1
```
lee: That looks RDMA-ish. Any recent MTU or jumbo frame changes on the ToR or host? We rolled a ToR config at 08:45 yesterday.
amir: I ran `ssh gpu-node-22 sudo ethtool -k eth0` — offload settings seem normal. `ip link show` shows MTU 9000 on hosts but ToR ports report 1500 for that leaf uplink in the config push logs. Oof.
kevin: MTU mismatch then. That explains fragmentation and pktloss under batching bursts where packet sizes hit jumbo thresholds. Causes reassembly + retransmits increasing latency.
sara: Any quick mitigation? We need to reduce customer impact for next 30m.
ops-oncall: We can do a targeted config change to bring host MTU down to 1500 on the two affected nodes, or roll back the ToR change. Which is faster?
lee: Rolling host MTU down is faster (no rack-level network change). But careful: some services assume 9k — ensure dataplane unaffected. I can run the host MTU change with a drain of local GPU jobs.
amir: Before doing that, confirm there aren't persisted RDMA QPs that will break. `rdma link show` + `ibstat` output from gpu-node-23: ```Port 1: LinkUp, speed 100Gb/s (expected)
Active MTU: 4096
Max MTU: 4096```
kevin: Active MTU 4096 on RDMA vs 1500 on ToR is a clear mismatch. Ops: schedule quick maintenance, but also set a temporary kube taint to avoid new batch assignments to those nodes.
ops-oncall: I'll taint gpu-node-22/23 now: `kubectl taint nodes gpu-node-22 node.kubernetes.io/maintenance=yes:NoSchedule` — done. :white_check_mark:
sara: Thanks. I'll watch the p95 dashboard and customer queues after that.
monitor-bot: alert: ew-p95-latency (gpu-node-22 <-> gpu-node-23) recovered from 118ms to 28ms after taint/drain action at 09:12 UTC.
lee: Plan for root cause postmortem: track the ToR config push at 08:45 (change id cfg-2023-08-45) that set uplink MTU to 1500, and host config drift that left hosts at 9k/4k. Need an automation check to align ToR/host MTUs, and a Canary that verifies RDMA MTU compatibility before config pushes.
sara: Agreed. Follow-ups: (1) permanent fix to reconcile MTU across leaf and hosts, (2) add a Grafana alert for RDMA Active MTU mismatch, (3) automation to check ToR push diffs for MTU changes. I'll open a tracking ticket.
amir: I'll attach packet captures and `tc -s qdisc` outputs to the ticket.
kevin: Also add a runbook entry: quick mitigation steps for live batching spikes (taint, drain, update MTU, rollback ToR).
sara: Great. Closing the thread here — thanks everyone. :heart:
